neighbours.label: ' by' after 'learn / understand (more) about X', where the next word is the act of study (by [studying / examining] …); the output promotes ' studying'. Other uses of ' by' stay quiet
fire: Doctors learn a great deal about the immune system by studying rare allergies.
You can understand more about a society by examining its prisons.
Geologists learn about the early Earth by studying ancient zircon crystals.
We discover more about how memory works by observing patients who have lost it.
Linguists learn a lot about grammar by studying the mistakes children make.
Astronomers understand more about our own sun by studying distant stars.
One can learn much about a period by reading its private letters.
Biologists learn more about ageing by studying animals that barely age.
quiet: Doctors save a great deal of time by sharing patient records.
You can reach the old prison by taking the coastal road.
The ancient zircon crystals were collected by a team of geologists.
The patients who had lost their memory were cared for by relatives.
Children make fewer grammar mistakes by the age of six.
Distant stars are catalogued by automated telescopes every night.
The private letters of the period were sold by the family.
Animals that barely age were described by early naturalists.

notes: Card: ' by', ' he', 'anthrop-ologist', ' from' at points where 'studying/studied' comes next; logit effect promotes ' studying', ' study', ' examine'. Probes: 'learn a lot about a healthy brain by' 0.51, 'understood about a language by' 0.41, 'sociologist' 0.70; 'save money by cooking' 0.01, 'designed by the engineer' 0.03, 'the villagers he studied' 0.11. The label covers the 'by' cases only; scholar titles (-ologist) also fire.
